source_name: MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank – Gazdálkodási adatok (financial data / annual reports)
why_relevant: Primary publication point for the Hungarian state development bank's audited IFRS individual and consolidated annual reports (ESEF), auditor reports and consolidated sustainability statements. MFB is the anchor actor of the state-owned/promotional lender cell and its reports carry lending volumes, group structure and operating-cost/procurement signals.
CRR 575/2013 Pillar-3 style disclosure of the development bank: capital, risk, exposures. Complements the annual report with structured, comparable risk data not present in press coverage.

Hungary's export-credit agency and export-import bank publishes audited IFRS individual and consolidated annual reports plus business/management reports. Key state-owned specialist lender; documents also disclose audit fees, headcount and IT/operating spend patterns.

State-backed SME credit-guarantee institution; publishes downloadable annual reports and audited financial statements. Guarantee volumes are a leading indicator of SME lending activity across the whole banking sector, and Garantiqa is an MFB Group member.

source_name: KAVOSZ Zrt. / Széchenyi Kártya Program – downloadable documents and announcements
why_relevant: KAVOSZ coordinates the state-subsidised Széchenyi Card SME lending programme distributed through partner banks. Its hirdetmények and product documentation reveal which banks distribute the programme, product terms and volume announcements — a strong proxy for SME credit channel structure. Its own statutory accounts are not on-site (see negative finding).

Largest surviving Hungarian home-savings institution (lakás-takarékpénztár), a specialised credit institution with ~10-13% share of residential housing lending. Company results/disclosure pages give annual figures, disbursement volumes and branch/agent-network signals.

Small values-based domestic commercial bank outside the top ten; publishes individual and consolidated annual reports on a dedicated disclosure page. Useful for tracking small-bank IT/branch strategy and vendor-relevant cost lines.

source_name: MTB Magyar Takarékszövetkezeti Bank – Konszolidált éves beszámolók (cooperative-sector legacy archive)
why_relevant: Legacy disclosure archive of the integrated savings-cooperative sector (Takarékbank/MTB) prior to the MBH consolidation. Essential for historical baselines on the cooperative branch network, integration IT spend and merger sequencing. Documents also mirrored on mbhbefektetesibank.hu.

source_name: MBH Jelzálogbank Nyrt. (ex-Takarék Jelzálogbank / FHB) – issuer disclosures
why_relevant: Specialist refinancing mortgage bank and mortgage-bond issuer; as a listed/regulated issuer it publishes annual reports, base prospectuses (alaptájékoztató) and supervisory decisions. Covers the specialist-lender slice of the cell and mortgage-funding structure.

source_name: BÉT / BSE company disclosure system (KIB – kibocsátói közzétételek)
why_relevant: Even non-listed specialist and state-owned lenders that issue bonds (MFB, Eximbank, Gránit, MBH Jelzálogbank) file audited annual reports and corrections here. It is the single richest pointer hub for finding the actual PDF of any Hungarian regulated financial issuer's annual report, including entities whose own websites are slow to publish.

source_name: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) – audit reports on state-owned financial institutions
why_relevant: The State Audit Office publishes full audit reports on state-owned lenders and guarantee schemes (e.g. a dedicated report on Garantiqa's guarantee activity). These reveal governance, IT/procurement and control weaknesses that annual reports omit — a high-signal, systematically under-used source for this cell.

source_name: Hiventures Kockázati Tőkealap-kezelő Zrt. – annual accounts / supplementary notes
why_relevant: MFB Group's state venture-capital arm; publishes its kiegészítő melléklet and accounts directly on site. Its notes also disclose MFB Group perimeter changes (e.g. Diákhitel Központ joining the group on 1 Oct 2024) — a rare structural signal about the state financial group.

source_name: MFB Csoport member-company map (MFB bankcsoport pages + Wikipedia MFB Csoport)
why_relevant: Enumerates the state financial group's members (Hiventures, Diákhitel Központ, Magyar Követeléskezelő, MFB Ingatlanfejlesztő, Garantiqa, Eximbank relationships), each of which files its own annual accounts. Turns one actor into a dozen collectible reporting entities.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség (Hungarian Leasing Association) – market statistics and reports
why_relevant: Publishes quarterly and annual new-business volumes, portfolio value, contract counts and customer-segment splits for the whole Hungarian leasing market. This is the aggregated frame around the leasing/consumer-finance arms in this cell, whose individual accounts are otherwise only on e-beszamolo.

source_name: Cofidis Magyarországi Fióktelepe – rendkívüli közlemények and business terms
why_relevant: Major foreign-owned consumer-finance actor operating in Hungary as a branch (fióktelep) plus a licensed bank entity (Magyar Cofidis Bank Zrt.). Branches do not publish standalone annual reports the way banks do, so the announcements and dated üzletszabályzat versions are the practical direct-disclosure stream; accounts come from e-beszamolo.

source_name: MBH Befektetési Bank – static file host mirroring legacy MTB/Takarék disclosures
why_relevant: Hosts both current investment-bank research (including equity reports on Gránit Bank) and mirrored legacy MTB/Takarékbank consolidated financial statements under /sw/static/file/ paths. Doubles as an analyst-report source on the smaller Hungarian lenders in this cell.

source_name: K-Monitor adatbázis – MFB and state-lender public-spending / contract records
why_relevant: NGO-curated archive linking state-owned financial institutions to public-money, contract and governance reporting. Reveals-indirectly category: surfaces procurement and vendor relationships around MFB and peers that never appear in the annual report narrative.
